{"answer":"Based on my search of the context filesystem, **yes, a new thread-type identifying parameter was proposed to be added** to the processing-exception-handler mechanism.

## Key Finding

The document **`discussions/kip-1270-process-exception-handler-global-thread.md`** explicitly discusses this design decision under **"LB2: Handler Awareness of Thread Type"** (lines 49-62):

### Proposed Solution (Option 1):
The design proposes introducing a **`ThreadType` (Stream or Global)** parameter to be included in the error handler context. This would allow a single `ProcessingExceptionHandler` to distinguish between:
- Errors from **global threads** (GlobalKTable processors)
- Errors from **regular stream threads** (KStream/KTable processors)

The document states:
> "**Solution**: Introduce `ThreadType` (Stream or Global) in errorHandlerContext"

This approach is described as **consistent with the existing `DeserializationExceptionHandler` pattern** and was presented as "Option 1" which was noted as "leaning toward" adoption based on the timeline (2026-01-23).

### Context
This proposal is part of **KIP-1270: Introduce ProcessExceptionalHandler for GlobalThread**, which aims to extend processing exception handling support to GlobalKTable processors that previously lacked configurable exception handling mechanisms.

{"error":null,"items":[{"lines":"49-63","path":"discussions/kip-1270-process-exception-handler-global-thread.md","score":25.526,"text":"### LB2: Handler Awareness of Thread Type (Open)
Two options for how handler distinguishes between stream types:

**Option 1**: Single Handler Configuration
- One `ProcessingExceptionHandler` handles all stream types (KStream, KTable, GlobalKTable)
- Consistent with existing `DeserializationExceptionHandler` pattern
- **Limitation**: Same handling behavior for all types (not flexible)
- **Solution**: Introduce `ThreadType` (Stream or Global) in errorHandlerContext

**Option 2**: Separate Optional Configuration
- New config: `global.processing.exception.handler` applies specifically to GlobalKTable
- If not configured, exceptions bubble up to uncaught exception handler (backward compatible)
- **Limitation**: Requires two configuration properties if users want different handlers
- **Advantage**: Handler always knows it's handling GlobalKTable errors
"},{"lines":"19-28","path":"discussions/kip-1270-process-exceptional-handler-global-thread.md","score":23.512,"text":"## Proposed Solution

Extend ProcessingExceptionHandler support to GlobalKTable processors, enabling consistent exception handling across all stream processing types.

After this KIP, when a processing exception occurs in a GlobalKTable processor:
- The configured ProcessingExceptionHandler.handleError() will be invoked
- If the handler returns Result.RESUME, processing continues with the next record
- If the handler returns Result.FAIL, the exception propagates (same as current behavior)
- If no handler is configured, behavior remains unchanged (backward compatible)
"},{"lines":"14-20","path":"discussions/kip-1270-process-exception-handler-globalthread.md","score":21.809,"text":"## Problem
When a processing exception occurs in a GlobalKTable processor:
- Exception propagates to GlobalStreamThread
- GlobalStreamThread terminates
- Entire Kafka Streams application shuts down
- No user-configurable exception handling available
"},{"lines":"23-30","path":"discussions/kip-1270-process-exception-handler-global-thread.md","score":21.295,"text":"## Proposed Solution

Extend `ProcessingExceptionHandler` support to GlobalKTable processors:
- When an exception occurs, invoke `ProcessingExceptionHandler.handleError()`
- If handler returns `Result.RESUME`, processing continues with the next record
- If handler returns `Result.FAIL`, exception propagates (same as current behavior)
- If no handler configured, behavior remains unchanged (backward compatible)
"},{"lines":"71-76","path":"discussions/kip-1270-process-exception-handler-global-thread.md","score":20.743,"text":"## Key Questions Clarified

1. **handleError() vs. handle()**: handleError() will be used; backward compatibility via default implementation
2. **DLQ support**: Records logged but not sent for GlobalKTable; future KIP for full support
3. **Configuration**: Leaning toward Option 1 (single handler) with ThreadType in context
"},{"lines":"11-18","path":"discussions/kip-1270-process-exceptional-handler-global-thread.md","score":20.593,"text":"## Problem

When a processing exception occurs in a GlobalKTable processor:
- The exception propagates to GlobalStreamThread
- The GlobalStreamThread terminates

"},{"lines":"13-22","path":"discussions/kip-1270-process-exception-handler-global-thread.md","score":19.062,"text":"## Problem

When a processing exception occurs in a GlobalKTable processor:
- The exception propagates to GlobalStreamThread
- The GlobalStreamThread terminates
- The entire Kafka Streams application shuts down
- No user-configurable exception handling is available

This contrasts with regular KStream/KTable processors which support `ProcessingExceptionHandler` for graceful error handling.
"},{"lines":"21-27","path":"discussions/kip-1270-process-exception-handler-globalthread.md","score":16.856,"text":"## Proposed Solution
After this KIP, exception handling becomes consistent:
- Configured ProcessingExceptionHandler.handleError() is invoked
- If handler returns Result.RESUME: processing continues with next record
- If handler returns Result.FAIL: exception propagates (current behavior)
- If no handler configured: behavior unchanged (backward compatible)
"},{"lines":"45-48","path":"discussions/kip-1270-process-exception-handler-global-thread.md","score":15.69,"text":"### LB1: DLQ Record Logging (Closed)

"},{"lines":"64-70","path":"discussions/kip-1270-process-exception-handler-global-thread.md","score":13.427,"text":"## DLQ Limitation

GlobalThread lacks producer infrastructure, so:
- DLQ records cannot be sent to Kafka topics
- Records are logged with full metadata instead
- Future KIP will address full DLQ support for GlobalKTable (requires adding Producer infrastructure)
